title: Without Backbiting
note: He defines this as not running people down when they aren’t there. Faults of speech grow from faults of the mind, so it follows the chapters on envy and coveting.

couplets.plain: Even if someone never speaks of righteousness and does wrong, it is good to have it said that they don’t backbite.
couplets.pm: Even if someone does nothing that is called righteous and commits sins, it is good for the world to say of them that they don’t backbite. This virtue isn’t dragged down by those faults. It stands above them.

links.quote: it is good to have it said that they don’t backbite
links.reason: Not backbiting is so prized that it is good to be credited with it, even for one who does wrong.

couplets.plain: Worse than destroying righteousness and doing wrong is to ruin someone behind their back and smile falsely to their face.
couplets.pm: To say there is no such thing as righteousness and then commit sins is bad. Worse is to ruin someone with scorn when they aren’t there, and smile falsely with them when they are. To ruin here is to put out a person’s brightness.

links.quote: ruin someone behind their back and smile falsely to their face

couplets.plain: Better to die than to live by backbiting and lies. Death brings the gain righteousness speaks of.
couplets.pm: Someone who runs others down behind their backs and puts on false sweetness to their faces would do better to die without doing so. Death ends the backbiting and the lying, and so brings the reward the books of righteousness speak of, which those who give it up gain in the next life.
couplets.sensitive: calls death better than a life of lies

links.reason: A life propped up by backbiting is rated lower than dying.

links.quote: Better to die than to live by backbiting and lies
links.reason: Lying is named alongside backbiting as a living not worth keeping.

couplets.plain: Even if you speak to someone’s face without mercy, don’t speak when they aren’t there, with no thought for what follows.
couplets.pm: Even if you have spoken to someone’s face with no regard for them, don’t, when they aren’t in front of you, say words that take no account of the fault that follows.
couplets.sensitive: urges silence about one who insults you

links.quote: don’t speak when they aren’t there

couplets.plain: That someone’s heart isn’t in the righteousness they talk of can be seen from the meanness of their backbiting.
couplets.pm: A backbiter may call righteousness good, but the mean mind that makes them backbite shows they aren’t saying it from the heart. The mind is bad, so the words can’t be accepted.

links.reason: Backbiting gives away the small heart behind someone’s talk of righteousness.

couplets.plain: Whoever tells another’s faults will have their own picked out with care and told.
couplets.pm: Whoever tells another’s faults behind that person’s back will have their own told in return. From their many faults, the ones that sting will be picked out. The person who hears of the backbiting goes further, finds the faults that will hurt most, and says them to the backbiter’s face.

links.quote: will have their own picked out with care and told
links.reason: Telling another’s faults invites having your own picked out and told.

couplets.plain: Those who can’t make friends with words that bring smiles will speak words that divide, and drive friends apart.
couplets.pm: Those who don’t know how to make friends among strangers with sweet words that bring people together will backbite until even their own kin leave them. To a backbiter, everyone becomes an enemy.
couplets.note: பிரிப்பர் can mean parting friends from one another. He takes it as driving the speaker’s own kin away from the speaker.

links.quote: speak words that divide, and drive friends apart
make friends with words that bring smiles
links.reason: Lacking the art of words that bring smiles is what turns a person into a splitter of friends.

couplets.plain: If it is their way to spread even the faults of those close to them, what will they do to strangers?
couplets.pm: If it is someone’s nature to spread the faults of people close to them behind their backs, what will they do to strangers? To spread is to make many people know, and nothing is crueller than that. Some read என்னர்கொல், “what sort of people are they?”

links.quote: spread even the faults of those close to them
links.reason: One who spreads the faults of those close will spare no one else.

couplets.plain: Is it for righteousness’ sake that the earth bears the weight of someone who waits for your back to speak mean words?
couplets.pm: Someone waits until others have gone and then speaks ill of them. The earth seems to carry that body thinking, “To bear this cruel thing is my righteousness.” It bears everything by nature, but this is hard to bear, so he says it does so for righteousness’ sake.

links.quote: the earth bears the weight of someone who waits for your back to speak mean words
links.reason: The backbiter’s very weight is treated as something hard to bear.
The earth is pictured as bearing the backbiter’s weight only for righteousness’ sake.

couplets.plain: If you could see your own faults as you see strangers’ faults, could any harm come to the enduring soul?
couplets.pm: Backbiters see the faults of strangers. If they could see their own fault of backbiting in the same way, could any suffering come to the lasting soul? Standing fair and seeing both alike is hard, hence “could”. Once seen, the fault stops, so there is no sin and no suffering in births to come.

links.quote: see your own faults as you see strangers’ faults
links.reason: Asks for the same scrutiny of yourself that you gladly give a stranger.
